attribution.note: Marcus's own bullet in his own post. He cites others' examples, but the claim that lots of errors are being reported is his.

semantics.note: Keeps 'are being reported', 'same as ever' and the named Rosenzweig example. Correctly leaves out the separate Riley hallucination sentence.

contract.note: Reading 'lots' as several identifiable reports, and 'same as ever' as familiar error types rather than unchanged rates, is a fair and ordinary plain reading.

evidence.note: A dated May 13 report of a GPT-4o reasoning failure. That is one report only. It does not verify Rosenzweig's example, and its timing relative to the post is not established.

reviews.rationale: The packet has one launch-day report of a GPT-4o error, from Riley. Under the contract, one report is not enough to show 'lots'. Rosenzweig's example was not recovered. There is no counterevidence, so the claim cannot be called contradicted, and the evidence does not settle the abundance it asserts.

attribution.note: Marcus's own description of the figure, in his own post.

contract.note: Reading 'not a lot' and 'not hugely' as generally modest gains in the displayed benchmarks is fair. No threshold is invented.

reviews.rationale: The benchmark figure the claim is about was not recovered. The only item is OpenAI's broad 'GPT-4 level' description, which is context. Without the figure's scores, neither comparison can be checked, so the claim is unresolved.

attribution.note: Marcus's own bullet in his own post.

semantics.note: Adding 'since GPT-4' is a reasonable reading of the implicit 14-month reference point. Otherwise faithful.

contract.note: Reading 'have' as possessing a completed model, not merely public release, fits his previous bullet ('if they had GPT-5, they would have shown it'). Fair.
